h1: The 6 Best Printers Under $150 for Home and Small Offices, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 printers under $150 including laser and inkjet all-in-ones, scored on running cost, duplex, scanning, wireless and ease of use.
summary: The Brother HL-L2405W is the best budget printer for text, a compact wireless monochrome laser that avoids the dried-ink problem. The Canon LBP6030w is the lower-priced laser alternative, the Canon PIXMA TR4720 is the all-in-one with a document feeder and fax, and the PIXMA TS6520 and TS4320 add color and duplex for families.
intro: The sticker price of a cheap printer is the smaller part of the bill. Most printers in this range are sold at or near cost, and the manufacturer earns its margin on the ink or toner that follows. A printer that costs less than $100 can cost more than that every year in cartridges if you print often, while a slightly dearer laser can run for years on a single toner. Before you look at features, decide how much you print and whether you need color.

We ranked six printers under $150 on running cost, print quality for the job, duplex printing, scanning, wireless setup and size. We reviewed manufacturer listings, which state the engine type and functions but rarely a cost per page, so we explain the logic rather than quote figures. One listing sits near the top of the price bracket, so check the current price before ordering.

products.name: Brother HL-L2405W Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A compact wireless laser that prints black-and-white text without the cost of ink.
products.description:
The Brother HL-L2405W is a compact monochrome laser printer with wireless and mobile printing and Alexa support. It prints only, with no scanning or copying. It sits near the top of the $100 to $200 bracket.

It wins because a laser printer is the best answer for most home offices that print text. Toner does not dry out the way inkjet ink can, so a printer that sits unused for weeks still works, and a toner cartridge prints many more pages. Wireless and mobile printing make setup straightforward, and the compact body fits on a shelf. The lack of a scanner and color are the trade-offs. Check the price against the $150 limit before buying.

Buy it for a household or small office that prints documents, forms and school work. Pair it with a phone scanning app for the occasional scan.
pros: Laser toner does not dry out
products.idealFor: Home offices printing mostly black-and-white text documents.
products.skipIf: You need color or a scanner in the same machine.

products.name: Canon imageCLASS LBP6030w Compact Wireless Laser Printer
products.verdict: A lower-priced wireless mono laser rated up to 19 pages per minute.
products.description:
The Canon imageCLASS LBP6030w is a monochrome laser printer rated up to 19 pages per minute, print only, with wireless connectivity and a compact footprint. It comes with a one-year limited warranty and is priced at $50 to $100.

It takes second place because it gives the laser benefits for less than the Brother. Nineteen pages a minute is a good speed for a home printer, and the compact body fits on a bookshelf. The price difference is the main appeal, but the listing is brief on mobile printing and setup features. A one-year warranty is standard.

Choose it if you want a laser printer for text at the lowest price. If you value Alexa or mobile apps, the Brother adds them.
pros: Laser printing at a lower price
products.idealFor: Budget-conscious buyers who want laser economics without the higher Brother price.
products.skipIf: You need to scan or print in color.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: A color inkjet that prints, scans, copies and faxes, with an automatic document feeder.
products.description:
The PIXMA TR4720 is a color inkjet all-in-one that prints, scans, copies and faxes. It has an automatic document feeder, mobile printing support and wireless connectivity in a compact design. The street range is $50 to $100.

Third place goes to it because the automatic document feeder and fax are rare at this price. A feeder lets you scan or copy a multi-page document without lifting the lid for each sheet, which saves time with tax papers and forms. The cost is the inkjet's running expense and the risk that ink dries out if the printer sits idle. Print quality is good for documents and photos at everyday sizes.

Buy it for a home office that scans paperwork and still sends the odd fax. If you print rarely, a laser avoids dried ink.
pros: Prints, scans and copies in color
cons: Ink can dry out if idle
products.idealFor: Home offices needing fax and document feeding without spending near the full budget.
products.skipIf: You print rarely and want to avoid dried ink.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A color all-in-one with automatic duplex and a 1.42 inch OLED display.
products.description:
The PIXMA TS6520 is a color inkjet all-in-one that prints, scans and copies, with two-sided printing handled by the machine, plus a small OLED screen (1.42 inches) and a simple button layout. Compact, and sold at $50 to $100.

Fourth place suits it because the OLED display and panel are the easiest to use in this group, which matters for a shared family printer. Automatic duplex halves paper use on documents. It lacks the TR4720's document feeder, so multi-page scanning is manual. Like any inkjet, it needs regular use to keep nozzles clear.

Choose it if you want the simplest day-to-day control and automatic two-sided printing. For heavy text, a laser is cheaper per page.
pros: Prints, scans and copies in color
products.idealFor: Home users who want the easiest day-to-day control panel experience.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A basic color all-in-one with automatic duplex and an easy setup process.
products.description:
The PIXMA TS4320 prints in color, scans and copies, flips pages for two-sided output on its own, connects wirelessly and is billed as quick to set up. Look for $50 to $100.

Fifth place fits because it gives you duplex and color at the lowest practical price, without the OLED display of the TS6520. Easy setup is its quiet strength, which suits a buyer who just wants a printer working in minutes. It is a plain machine, and features such as a feeder and fax are absent.

Buy it for a student or a family that wants color and duplex on a budget. Print something weekly to keep the ink healthy.
pros: Automatic duplex at a low price
products.idealFor: Buyers who want duplex printing while spending the least under $150.
products.skipIf: You need a feeder or faster printing.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A budget color all-in-one that includes a 3-month Instant Ink trial.
products.description:
The HP DeskJet 4355 is a wireless color inkjet all-in-one that prints, scans and copies, in a compact body. It includes a three-month Instant Ink trial and has AI-capable printing features. Typical pricing runs $50 to $100.

Last place follows because the listing highlights a subscription trial rather than a feature that lowers cost. Instant Ink is a paid plan that sends cartridges based on pages printed, and it can be good value for steady printers but is wasted on light ones. Check how the printer treats third-party cartridges and what happens when you cancel the plan. It has no duplex listed, and print speeds are not stated.

Buy it for light home printing when the lowest price counts. Read the subscription terms before you enroll.
products.idealFor: Light home printing where saving budget matters most.
products.skipIf: You print a lot or want to avoid subscriptions.

methodology.title: Running cost
methodology.description: We weighed laser against inkjet for cost per page and idle reliability, since ink and toner outweigh the purchase price.

methodology.title: Functions
methodology.description: We compared print, scan, copy and fax, and noted automatic document feeders, which save time on multi-page jobs.

methodology.title: Duplex and speed
methodology.description: We looked at automatic two-sided printing and stated speeds, which affect paper use and waiting.

methodology.title: Setup and controls
methodology.description: We considered wireless setup, mobile printing and the clarity of the control panel.

methodology.title: Price and warranty
methodology.description: We checked each price bracket against the $150 limit and noted warranty terms where stated.

whatMatters.detail: Laser printers use toner powder that does not dry out, and a cartridge prints many pages. Inkjets print color and photos and can scan, but ink costs more per page and can clog if unused. Choose laser for text and inkjet for color.

Cost per page is cartridge price divided by pages printed. It is the biggest factor over time, and low-end inkjets often have high ones. Check the cartridge model and its stated page yield on the manufacturer's page before buying.
Duplex prints on both sides of the paper without you flipping the sheet. It halves paper use for documents. Look for automatic duplex in the specs, since manual duplex means you reload the pages.
An automatic document feeder pulls sheets through the scanner one by one. It is valuable for multi-page scans and copies. Look for ADF on the listing, which is rare under $150.

Some printers push ink subscriptions and may limit third-party cartridges. These plans can save money for heavy printers and cost more for light ones. Read the terms and check whether you can print without enrolling.

cards.text: Reliable wireless setup, low cost per page for essays and handouts, and duplex to save paper. Color is helpful for projects.

cards.text: The Brother HL-L2405W is the best for essays, and the Canon PIXMA TS4320 gives color and duplex at the lowest cost.

faq.q: Do these printers work with a phone?
faq.a: Yes, all list wireless printing, and the Brother and Canon PIXMA TR4720 mention mobile printing support. Install the maker's app and connect to your home network. Setup takes a few minutes.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with cheap printers?
faq.a: Ignoring ink or toner cost. A cheap printer with expensive cartridges costs more over time. Check cartridge prices and yields before you buy.

faq.q: Is a laser printer worth it over an inkjet?
faq.a: For text it is, because toner is cheaper per page and does not dry out. Inkjets win for color and photos and for scanning. If you print once a month, a laser avoids clogged ink.

faq.q: How do I keep ink from drying out?
faq.a: Print a page or run a nozzle check every week or two. Keep the printer powered by turning it off with the power button, which caps the heads. Leaving it unused for months risks clogs.
Often, but policies vary, and some printers reject them or warn. Check the maker's current policy and the cartridge compatibility. Genuine cartridges are the safe, if dearer, option.

faq.q: Do I need a scanner in a printer?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Many people scan with a phone app, which works well for occasional documents. If you scan often, an all-in-one with a feeder saves time.

finalTake: The Brother HL-L2405W is the best printer under $150 for most people who print text, thanks to cheap toner and no dried-ink problems. The Canon LBP6030w is the lower-cost laser, the TR4720 suits home offices with scanning and fax, and the TS6520 and TS4320 suit families that need color and duplex.
